## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best tide.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind: a NW-quadrant offshore (profile 320) is supported by Surf-Forecast (NNW), Indonesian Surf Guide (N-W) and Padang Padang Surf Camp's Uluwatu page ('NW monsoon'). The same camp is inconsistent elsewhere. Its Keramas page lists 'E or NE light to moderate' as the wind (not labelled offshore, so no value), and its FAQ says the SW-W monsoon is offshore at east-facing breaks (247.5, contradicting). Both the camp and the FAQ credit a cold morning mountain (Agung) wind as offshore, with no compass direction. So wind support is moderate, with one publisher contradicting itself. Swell direction: S-SSW is well supported (195-205 from the surf camp; SSW from Surf-Forecast; S/SW from WSL and Surfing-Waves; SE-S from Surf Atlas). WSL's 'west' goes beyond the profile window. Size: 3-10 ft from WSL, Surfing-Waves and the surf camp (2-10 ft) matches the profile. Tide conflicts. Mid to high: WannaSurf, WSL, Surfing-Waves; high: Indonesian Surf Guide. Mid only, with high tide rejected: Padang Padang Surf Camp (the FAQ just says mid). Surfing-Waves contradicts itself with 'mid to low'; Surf Atlas says only avoid dead low. Season: the wet season (November/December-March/April) is now from four publishers, consistent with the profile. Period: no numeric working range. The surf camp says 20 s swells arrive smaller than 14 s ones but barrel harder, and Surf Atlas says long periods, qualitatively. Bathymetry: descriptive only (lava/volcanic rock reef, rivermouth sediment bulge, a ridge with channels either side). No measured survey or peer-reviewed study found (Crossref: only social-science papers for Keramas village). The three Padang Padang Surf Camp entries (Keramas page, Uluwatu page remark, FAQ) are one publisher.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages, one publisher) says 195-205 deg gives the best results, Surf-Forecast gives SSW (202.5 deg) as ideal, and Surfing-Waves gives south and southwest as ideal.
  - S6 (Padang Padang Surf Camp (balisurfingcamp.com)): “For Keramas, the more southerly end of that range, closer to 195°–205°, produces the best results”
  - S8 (Padang Padang Surf Camp (balisurfingcamp.com)): “Keramas performs best on 195°–205°”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “the ideal swell direction is from the south southwest”
  - S10 (Surfing-Waves.com): “The ideal swell directions are from the south and south west”
- **Acceptable range**: WSL says Keramas likes south, southwest and west swells (180-270 deg) and Surf Atlas says the rivermouth bulge harnesses SE and S swell sets (135-180 deg); the value spans both, and the Indonesian Surf Guide says it breaks on all swell directions.
  - S3 (World Surf League): “Keramas, like most of Bali, likes south, southwest and west swells.”
  - S9 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “harnesses any SE, S swell sets into those plump shoulders”
  - S5 (Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Keremas breaks from waist high to double overhead, all swell directions and is offshore in N – W winds.”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break, and WannaSurf says that because it is very far up the island you need a large swell to be moving through.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Keramas in Sanur - Bali is an exposed reef break”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “given that its very far up the island you need a large swell to be moving through”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft and WSL that it holds waves from 3 ft, while Padang Padang Surf Camp says it is surfable from around 2 ft and the Indonesian Surf Guide from waist high; no source states whether its feet are face or offshore heights.
- **Swell height · ideal range**: Padang Padang Surf Camp gives 4-6 ft as the sweet spot for most surfers and Surfing-Waves says best from 3 to 10 ft, while Surf Atlas says it fires at its finest at 8 ft+ with long periods and is an everyday wave between 3 and 8 ft.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast gives north-northwest, the Indonesian Surf Guide N to W, and one Padang Padang Surf Camp page the NW monsoon as offshore, while the same publisher's FAQ says the SW to W monsoon is offshore at east-facing breaks; the camp also says a cold mountain wind is offshore almost every day, without a direction.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WannaSurf, WSL and Surfing-Waves say mid to high, the Indonesian Surf Guide says it needs a high tide, Padang Padang Surf Camp says mid tide (two pages), Surfing-Waves elsewhere says mid to low, and Surf Atlas says wait until at least an hour past low.
